newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to reopen Chernobyl reactor in a year.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to reopen Chernobyl reactor in a year.

text.p: Ukraine, which last month closed the Chernobyl nuclear station's first reactor, said on Friday it plans next year to reopen another Chernobyl unit which was shut down in 1991 because of a fire.
"It is due to be switched on in the final quarter of next year," Viktor Chebrov, the head of the Derzhkmotom state nuclear authority, told a news conference.
"We still have to do some work to improve the safety of the reactor," he added.

Chebrov said the move would not violate Kiev's pledge to the international community to close the entire station by 2000. The Group of Seven (G7) rich industrial nations has promised $3.1 billion in credits and grants in return for the closure.

The first reactor at Chernobyl was switched off late last month as part of a promise made by President Leonid Kuchma to close the entire station. The fourth reactor exploded in 1986 and sent clouds of radiation across Europe.
The third reactor is still in operation, and the second was closed in 1991 after it caught fire.
